What does the fitted response time mean in the s-plane?

The fitted model has one pole, at $s=-1/\tau$ (with $\tau$ in seconds), and $$H(s)=\frac{1}{\tau s+1}.$$ Slide the multiplier to try other values of $\tau$ on fixed axes. Larger $\tau$ moves the pole toward zero and slows the temperature response. $H(s)$ maps ambient changes to package temperature with zero initial deviation; it is not the transform of the full cooling record. Changing the dataset, ambient temperature or training split refits the baseline and resets the multiplier.

The top results always use the training-fitted baseline. Trying settings against later measurements is exploration: choosing a value using these errors would use those measurements for tuning.

Separate illustrative scenario

What would a delayed shipment do?

Assumed parameters for a single-temperature package in constant surroundings. This scenario does not reuse the fitted beaker parameters. Stages, return trips and the full continue/caution/return/replace decision are in Simulate; both pages use the same margin classifier. This simplified panel has its own explicit buffer and checks only the upper limit. Use matching settings for comparisons.

This panel evaluates an upper temperature limit only. Green: margin meets the selected buffer. Yellow: margin is non-negative but below the buffer. Fuchsia: an excursion is predicted. A temperature exactly at the limit is within range; a zero arrival margin is caution when the buffer is positive. It does not assess lower-limit excursions, pharmaceutical stability, varying surroundings, or separate container and payload temperatures.
